metadata.source: Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails v2.0
metadata.intendedFor: Cloud architecture review for Protected B / Medium workloads under TBS / SSC mandate

rules.naturalLanguage: Strong, phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication must be implemented for all administrative user accounts. The mechanism must be explicitly identified (FIDO2, PIV-derived, or smart card MFA).
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to explicitly identify a phishing-resistant MFA mechanism (e.g., FIDO2 security keys, PIV-derived credentials, or smart-card MFA) for all administrative accounts, per GC Cloud Guardrail 01.
rules.evidenceQuote: Implement strong multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all user accounts. Use phishing resistant MFA where and when available.
rules.sourceContent: Implement strong multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all user accounts. Use phishing resistant MFA where and when available. User accounts and identities include: root or global administrator (as it has enhanced or the highest level of privilege over the control plane and addresses all aspects of access control).

rules.naturalLanguage: Sensitive electronic information categorised Protected B, Protected C or Classified must be hosted within the geographic boundaries of Canada (or a GC mission abroad). The architecture must commit to a Canadian data-centre region.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("Canada Central") || input1.text.Contains("Canada East") || input1.text.Contains("hosted in Canada") || input1.text.Contains("Toronto") || input1.text.Contains("Montreal") || input1.text.Contains("Quebec")) && !input1.text.Contains("US East") && !input1.text.Contains("US West")
rules.remediation: Replace the {section.heading} clause with: "All Protected B workloads shall reside in a Canadian data-centre region (e.g., Canada Central / Canada East), per Directive on Service and Digital subsection 4.4.3.14 and GC Cloud Guardrail 05."
rules.evidenceQuote: Demonstrate that the service location is within Canada for all Protected B cloud services where configurable.
rules.sourceContent: According to subsection 4.4.3.14 of the Directive on Service and Digital: 'Ensuring computing facilities located within the geographic boundaries of Canada or within the premises of a Government of Canada department located abroad, such as a diplomatic or consular mission, be identified and evaluated as a principal delivery option for all sensitive electronic information and data under government control that has been categorized as Protected B, Protected C or is Classified.'

rules.naturalLanguage: Data at rest must be encrypted using CSE-approved cryptographic algorithms (per ITSP.40.111). The architecture must reference an approved algorithm (AES-256) and FIPS 140 validation status.
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to commit to AES-256 encryption with a FIPS 140-2 (or 140-3) validated cryptographic module, aligned with CSE ITSP.40.111 and GC Cloud Guardrail 06.
rules.evidenceQuote: Use cryptographic algorithms and protocols approved by Communications Security Establishment Canada (CSE) in accordance with ITSP.40.111 and ITSP.40.062.
rules.sourceContent: Implement an encryption mechanism to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data when data is at rest in storage. Use cryptographic algorithms and protocols approved by Communications Security Establishment Canada (CSE) in accordance with ITSP.40.111 and ITSP.40.062.

rules.naturalLanguage: Data in transit must be encrypted by default using TLS 1.2 or higher. The architecture must explicitly commit to TLS 1.2+ for all cloud services and external communications.
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 for all in-transit traffic and explicitly disable TLS 1.0 / 1.1, per GC Cloud Guardrail 07 and the GC Web Sites and Services Management Configuration Requirements.
rules.evidenceQuote: Encrypt data in transit by default (for example, Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2) to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data, including for all publicly accessible sites and external communications.
rules.sourceContent: Encrypt data in transit by default (for example, Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2) to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data, including for all publicly accessible sites and external communications. Use CSE-approved cryptographic algorithms and protocols in accordance with ITSP.40.111 and ITSP.40.062.

rules.naturalLanguage: Audit logging must be enabled for the cloud environment and workloads, with sign-in, configuration-change, and resource-provisioning events captured, and a defined retention period.
rules.lambda: input1.text.Contains("audit log") && (input1.text.Contains("365 days") || input1.text.Contains("12 months") || input1.text.Contains("3 years") || input1.text.Contains("7 years") || input1.text.Contains("year")) && (input1.text.Contains("sign-in") || input1.text.Contains("configuration change") || input1.text.Contains("resource provisioning"))
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to commit to a defined retention period (e.g., 365 days minimum) and to capture sign-in, configuration-change, and resource-provisioning events, per GC Cloud Guardrail 11 and the GC Event Logging Guidance.
rules.evidenceQuote: Confirm that the following logs are included: Sign-in logs (interactive and non-interactive sign-ins, API sign-ins); Access privilege and group changes; Changes in configuration of the cloud platform; Cloud resource provisioning activities.
rules.sourceContent: Implement adequate level of logging and reporting, including a security audit log function in all information systems. Configure events within the solution to support security monitoring, in accordance with the GC Event Logging Guidance.
